title: A finite-type geometrically connected geometrically normal scheme is geometrically integral
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a nonempty scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change]. Assume that $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$, meaning that $|X_K|$ is connected for every such extension [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-connected-scheme], and geometrically normal over $k$, meaning that every local ring of every $X_K$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $X$ is geometrically integral over $k$: $X_K$ is integral for every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Tag 033M, lemma-normal-Noetherian, applied to the finite-type field base changes; this is the final connected-normal component argument of more-morphisms.tex, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary field extension $K/k$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2), the projection $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is of finite type. In particular it is locally of finite type and $X_K$ is quasi-compact: apply the quasi-compactness clause of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] to the whole affine target. Every ideal of the field $K$ is either zero or the whole field (a nonzero element is invertible), so every ideal is finitely generated and $K$ is Noetherian. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally Noetherian by its one-chart affine cover [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Applying [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives that $X_K$ is locally Noetherian. Together with the quasi-compactness just proved, this makes $X_K$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type) and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); the field is Noetherian by the elementary ideal argument written here.

proof.text: Geometric normality gives normal-domain local rings at every point of $X_K$. Apply clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to the Noetherian scheme of step 1: $X_K$ is a finite disjoint union of clopen normal integral components. By geometric connectedness and [def-weil-connected-scheme], $X_K$ is nonempty and connected. Choose a point and the component $C$ containing it in that decomposition. The clopen sets $C$ and $X_K\setminus C$ partition $X_K$, so connectedness and the nonemptiness of $C$ force $X_K\setminus C$ to be empty. Hence $X_K=C$ with its open subscheme structure, and is integral.

source.place: Tag 033M, lemma-normal-Noetherian; the final connected-normal argument of more-morphisms.tex, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type (Tag 057K).

proof.text: The extension $K/k$ was arbitrary. Step 2 therefore proves that $X_K$ is integral for every field extension $K/k$, which is exactly geometric integrality in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].
